reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes a cryptocurrency arbitrage method using Biftex and Binance, claiming substantial returns from Ethereum price differences. It directs viewers to deposit ETH into a wallet and move cryptocurrency through exchange and withdrawal forms while encouraging them to try the scheme. The evidence does not verify whether the displayed balances, rates, withdrawals, or returns are genuine or reproducible.

citations.quote: Today I will show you how to earn 10% on Ethereum arbitrage using the Biftex exchange.
Go to the deposit and replenish our Ethereum wallet.
Go to trading, select Ethereum,. Enter the entire amount and click sell.
Try it yourself according to this scheme.
In this video I show how I earned over $500 on the new biftex exchange by making a deposit in ETH coin and exchanging it into usdt.

opening.argument: The presentation uses instructional, conditional language rather than a promise that viewers will receive a fixed return. It says it will show a method for earning “10%,” describes a personal result, and presents the steps as something viewers may try, but it does not state that success is guaranteed or that losses are impossible. The screen also shows a normal trading interface and a withdrawal marked as processing, which is consistent with an example of a transaction rather than proof of guaranteed income. A careful viewer is therefore given a method to evaluate, not an assurance that the outcome is certain.

citations.quote: Today I will show you how to earn 10% on Ethereum arbitrage using the Biftex exchange.
We earned $1,000 in one round with such a simple. Method.
You can work as much as you like. Have a nice day.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The cited language shows a claimed result and instructions, but it does not establish a guarantee, a required payment to the creator, or a promise that every viewer will earn the same amount. “Try it yourself” is compatible with inviting independent evaluation of a trading method. The prosecution also concedes that the displayed balances, rates, withdrawals, and returns are not verified; that uncertainty cannot itself prove deceptive intent.

citations.quote: Try it yourself according to this scheme.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The absence of the word “guarantee” does not remove the persuasive return claim. The speaker says viewers can earn 10%, reports earning $1,000 in one round, and tells them to replenish an Ethereum wallet. The processing screen shows an attempted withdrawal, not successful receipt, so it does not substantiate the promoted outcome.

citations.quote: Today I will show you how to earn 10% on Ethereum arbitrage using the Biftex exchange.
Go to the deposit and replenish our Ethereum wallet.

opening.argument: The primary format is a step-by-step operational demonstration of exchange functions. The narration walks through depositing Ethereum, selecting the asset, selling it, and initiating a withdrawal, while the sampled frames show an ETH/BUSD market, a sell form, and a withdrawal-processing dialog. That is concrete instruction about how an exchange workflow operates. Demonstrating a claimed personal example does not by itself turn educational material into a scam, especially where the evidence does not establish that the interface, transaction, or return was fabricated.

citations.quote: Go to trading, select Ethereum,. Enter the entire amount and click sell.
Waiting for confirmation of the. Transaction in the blockchain.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution’s own description identifies a workflow, but a workflow can be instructional without being deceptive. Showing where to deposit, trade, and withdraw explains operation; it does not establish that the creator collected funds, controlled viewers’ accounts, or concealed an inability to withdraw. The reference argument relies on the possibility that the demonstration is unverified, rather than evidence that it is false.

citations.quote: Go to the deposit and replenish our Ethereum wallet.
Click withdraw now.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The tutorial framing is inseparable from its promotion of returns. It opens by saying viewers can earn 10%, reports nearly $1,000, and closes by telling them to try the scheme. The visible trading and withdrawal controls establish only that screens exist; they do not prove that the claimed arbitrage profit was real, transferable, or reproducible.

citations.quote: As you can see we have already earned. Almost $1,000
Try it yourself according to this scheme.

opening.argument: At most, this is promotion of ordinary cryptocurrency exchange services and a trading procedure. The description identifies one site for buying crypto and another for selling it, while the footage shows market controls, an Ethereum sell order, and a withdrawal form. The evidence does not show a downline, credential request, coercion, fabricated identity, or funds being sent to the speaker. Nor does a displayed processing status establish that the service is unsafe. Viewers are shown an external service and can assess it independently; the material does not demonstrate a scam mechanism.

citations.quote: Buy crypto - https://www.binance.com/ Sell crypto - https://biftex.com/

rebuttal.rebuttal: The reference side identifies deposits and withdrawals, but those are ordinary features of cryptocurrency exchanges and do not alone constitute a scam mechanism. The cited material does not show that the creator requests viewers’ credentials, receives their deposits, promises a downline, or guarantees a return. A claim that a price difference exists may be promotional, yet promotion of an external trading service is not proof that the service is fraudulent.

citations.quote: Buy crypto - https://www.binance.com/ Sell crypto - https://biftex.com/
Paste it here and. Enter the entire amount. Click withdraw now.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The issue is not whether deposits and withdrawals can be ordinary exchange functions. The video uses those functions to promote a method with unusually large claimed returns: it says the speaker earned over $500 and nearly $1,000, then directs viewers to fund the process. The withdrawal dialog says processing, while the record does not establish completed receipt, so the central profit claim remains unsupported.
